mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the federal funds rate (measured as a 3-month rolling decrease) signals an easing monetary policy, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with 3-month FEDFUNDS decline, or Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the unemployment rate rises above 5.5% (a threshold indicating labor market deterioration), it signals weakening economic conditions and triggers a flight to safety, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where UNRATE exceeds 5.5%, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) and a rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) signals stagflation, which erodes corporate profit margins and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where INDPRO declines and CPIAUCSL rises, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 105, it indicates robust manufacturing activity, which supports corporate earnings growth and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where INDPRO > 105, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in non-farm payroll employment (PAYEMS) signals strong labor market conditions, which boosts consumer spending and corporate revenues, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods with PAYEMS growth, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: When the core inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) rises above 2.5% annually, it signals persistent inflationary pressures that may prompt the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where CPIAUCSL > 2.5, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and a rise in consumer credit (RSAFS) signals a contraction in the housing market and increased consumer debt, which weakens the economic outlook and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in more than 55% of periods where HOUST declines and RSAFS rises, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of strong consumer spending (CPIAUCSL above 2.0% year-over-year), the S&P 500 tends to rise as corporate revenues grow, leading to positive forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods where CPIAUCSL > 2.0, or Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year window.
